verdict: Coca-Cola Europacific grew half-year sales 4.4% to $12.3B as it sold more drinks at slightly higher prices — and turned that into $1.1B of profit.

segments.name: Europe
segments.note: Bottling and selling Coca-Cola drinks across Europe — the bigger of the company's two regions. Revenue rose 5.9% from a year ago.

segments.name: Australia, Pacific & Southeast Asia
segments.note: The APS region, including Australia, Indonesia and the Philippines. Reported revenue rose just 0.4% because currency moves hid stronger local growth of 5.4%.

opex.name: Selling & distribution
opex.note: Getting drinks to shops, bars and restaurants — trucks, warehouses, sales teams and coolers.

opex.name: Administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, IT, legal and head-office costs.

opex.name: Other income
opex.note: Income outside day-to-day bottling — this half it includes a €23M gain on selling a property in Germany.

otherDetail: Net finance and non-operating costs were $136.2M: $169.4M of finance costs, less $35.5M of finance income, plus a $2.3M non-operating charge.
footerNote: CCEP reports half-yearly, so this report covers the six months ended Jul 3, 2026 — there is no standalone Q2 income statement. CCEP reports in euros (revenue €10,724M; profit after taxes €991M, of which €967M to owners of the parent). Dollar figures are converted at the ECB euro reference rate for the period-end date, €1 = $1.1448 on Jul 3, 2026. Lines are rounded after conversion, so converted totals may differ by a few $M from a direct conversion of the euro totals.
follow100Note: This is a half-year report: the $100 breakdown is per $100 of revenue for the six months ended Jul 3, 2026.
oneTimers: Reported costs include €44M of restructuring charges for business transformation. On the company's 'comparable' basis — leaving out such items — operating profit was €1,481M rather than the reported €1,458M.
Other income includes a €23M gain on the sale of a property in Germany.

takeaways.title: Steady growth in the first half
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 4.4% to €10.7B ($12.3B) for the six months. Volume grew 2.2% once adjusted for extra selling days, and revenue per case rose 0.4% — growth came from selling more drinks, not from big price rises. Full-year guidance was reaffirmed.

takeaways.title: Europe carried it; Asia was flat in euros
takeaways.text: Europe's revenue rose 5.9% to €7.9B. The APS region (Australia, Pacific and Southeast Asia) rose only 0.4% in euros to €2.8B, but grew 5.4% before currency effects — the euro's strength hid the local growth.

takeaways.title: Profit up, dividend set
takeaways.text: Profit after tax was €991M ($1.1B), up 5.8%, and diluted earnings per share rose 9.1% to €2.17. The company declared an interim dividend of €0.82 per share and generated €435M of comparable free cash flow in the half.
